reconcile.note: Keil & Delitzsch argue the Amram in Exodus 6 is a later namesake, not Kohath's literal son, so the short Levi-to-Moses list telescopes unstated generations.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen treats the Ephraim-to-Joshua line in 1 Chronicles 7 as an artificial late genealogy, of which its mismatch with the parallel Levi-Moses chain is one instance.

quotes.text: In the case of Ephraim a long and meagre genealogy…only is given, which, begun in vers. 20, 21, and continued in ver. 25, constantly repeats the same names (Tahath, Tahan, 1Samuel i. 1; Eladah, Laadan, Shuthelah, Telah), and finally reaches its end and goal in Joshua, whose father Nun alone is known to the older sources!
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on the artificiality of the Chronicler's genealogical lists.

sides.snippet: Amram took Jochebed his father's sister to himself as wife; and she bore him Aaron and Moses
sides.verseText: Amram took Jochebed his father's sister to himself as wife; and she bore him Aaron and Moses: and the years of the life of Amram were a hundred and thirty-seven years.

sides.snippet: Nun his son, Joshua his son
sides.verseText: Nun his son, Joshua his son.
